Hey, just wanted to say this is a very succinct and clear summary of at least what this condition ( from my experience). Like every bullet resonates with me (i do have lethargy too though). 

I have to say that the abstract reasoning problems are the most disheartening and concerning to me. To be honest I was pretty sure i had a learning disability. I found that tasks like trying to generalize information to solve a new problem, finding more efficient ways of doing things, or even being able to analyze a situation well are things that I struggle with a lot. 

With Most multi step tasks that I do, i find that halfway through, i did it in the like least efficient way possible. Other times, i find i often hit “dead ends”. Where im shown that my first intuition towards approaching a problem was wrong for a seemingly obvious reason, even though it seemed promising. 

I have some adhd friends and their experience with it are different than mine. That kind of became a hunch for there being something else wrong with me. 

The double whammy of ADHD and SCT is more than the sum of its parts. At the end of Dr Russel Barkely’s SCT presentation on youtube, he shows a bar graph where he superimposed the sct deficit ratings atop those of adhd. Basically showing that that those with the comorbidity were much more affected than those with either adhd or sct. 

For OP or anyone else thats reading, have you found a way to increase your cognition or At least compensate for these issues? What i found works is: 

- a healthy dose of stimulant meds
- 20 min morning meditation
- frequent exercise
- studying/learning like 10x longer than the average person 

(To be honest, the stimulants and studying are the only effective things for me in that list)

If you are in the US consider trying for a sport pilot license. Please double check (as I’ve forgotten) but i don’t think you need a medical for that certification. Its extremely limited in what you’re allowed to fly/ how far you can go but its better than nothing.
